Guides / Manufacturing

Batch Assembly (Two-Component)

An assembly model where two separate component streams must be joined before the assembly operation. A Batch block holds components until one of each type is available, then combines them for processing. Models kitting, assembly, or any multi-input synchronization.

When to use this

  • Modeling an assembly operation that requires one item from each of two or more component streams
  • Synchronizing multiple input streams before a combined processing step
  • Analyzing the impact of component imbalance on assembly throughput and WIP
  • Modeling kitting operations where a kit of parts must be assembled before production begins
  • Any scenario where items from multiple sources must be matched before proceeding

Blocks

BlockLibraryLabelPurpose
CreateItem.lbrComponentAGenerates component A items at the production or arrival rate for stream A
CreateItem.lbrComponentBGenerates component B items at the production or arrival rate for stream B
QueueItem.lbrBufferAHolds component A items waiting to be matched with a component B item for batching
QueueItem.lbrBufferBHolds component B items waiting to be matched with a component A item for batching
BatchItem.lbrAssemblerCollects one item from each connected input Queue and combines them into a single batched item for downstream processing
QueueItem.lbrAssemblyQueueHolds batched items waiting for the assembly Activity
ActivityItem.lbrAssemblyPerforms the assembly operation on the combined batch item
ExitItem.lbrFinishedProductCollects completed assemblies and records throughput

Connections

  • ComponentA (ItemOut) → BufferA (ItemIn)
  • ComponentB (ItemOut) → BufferB (ItemIn)
  • BufferA (ItemOut) → Assembler (ItemIn[0])
  • BufferB (ItemOut) → Assembler (ItemIn[1])
  • Assembler (ItemOut) → AssemblyQueue (ItemIn)
  • AssemblyQueue (ItemOut) → Assembly (ItemIn)
  • Assembly (ItemOut) → FinishedProduct (ItemIn)

Key parameters

BlockParameterTypicalWhat it controls
BatchbatchSize / batchTypebatchSize=1 per input (permanent batch of N=2), batchType=permanentFor assembly, use permanent batching (components are permanently combined). batchSize typically 1 per input connector. Temporary batching groups items that will be unbatched later.
Create (ComponentA)distribution / arg1Exponential, mean=3 minComponent A arrival rate. If rate differs significantly from component B, the slower stream becomes the bottleneck and the faster stream builds up in its buffer.
Create (ComponentB)distribution / arg1Exponential, mean=3 minComponent B arrival rate. Ideally balanced with component A rate. Imbalance causes one buffer to grow without bound.
BatchmatchAttributenull (no matching) or attribute nameIf components must be matched by a specific attribute (e.g., serial number or order ID), set matchAttribute. Without matching, Batch combines any available item from each input.

Common mistakes

  • Connecting component Create blocks directly to the Batch block without Queue buffers — the Batch block needs Queue blocks on each input because it pulls from Queue outputs, not directly from Create outputs; without Queues, components cannot accumulate and Batch will stall
  • Setting mismatched component arrival rates and not accounting for the resulting buffer imbalance — if component A arrives twice as fast as component B, the BufferA will grow indefinitely while BufferB stays near empty; always balance mean arrival rates across all component streams
  • Using temporary batch mode when permanent assembly is intended — temporary batching allows items to be unbatched later (via Unbatch block), which is wrong for assembly; use permanent batch mode when components are physically combined
  • Expecting Batch block throughput to exceed the rate of the slowest component stream — the assembly rate is limited by min(rateA, rateB); adding more Assembly Activities downstream cannot compensate for a slow component supplier

What to measure

  • Assembly throughput (limited by slower component stream)
  • Buffer length for each component stream (imbalance indicator)
  • Batch wait time (how long until matching component arrives)
  • Assembly Activity utilization
  • WIP ratio between BufferA and BufferB (large ratio indicates flow imbalance)
